title: No more ions than quanta
spoken: The number of ionized molecules is at most the absorbed energy divided by h times the frequency.
explanation: The absorbed energy divided by one quantum's energy is the number of quanta absorbed; if each ionizes at most one molecule, that number bounds the ions.
assumptions: One absorbed quantum ionizes at most one molecule.
These are modern teaching equations in SI notation, not a transcription of the printed paper.

notes.title: Number of ionized molecules
notes.explanation: Counted one by one. The paper counts gram-molecules, j.

notes.title: Light energy absorbed
notes.explanation: What the gas takes in; the paper prints it L.

notes.title: Planck's constant
notes.explanation: With the frequency, the size of one quantum.

notes.title: Frequency of the light
notes.explanation: Higher frequency means fewer, larger quanta for the same energy.

notes.title: At most one ion per quantum
notes.explanation: Energy that heats the gas instead produces no ions, so the count can fall short of the bound, never exceed it.
